question: What is the primary pump of the cardiovascular system?
explanation: The heart acts as the central muscular pump that drives blood through the vascular network. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is a continuous blood supply essential for human cells?

options.A: To deliver oxygen and remove cellular waste
options.B: To filter excess water from the bloodstream
options.C: To produce red bone marrow for immunity
options.D: To maintain a constant body temperature of 37 degrees

explanation: Cells require constant oxygen delivery and waste removal to survive and maintain normal metabolic function. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which layer of the heart wall is responsible for generating pumping pressure?
explanation: The myocardium consists of thick cardiac muscle tissue that contracts to pump blood out of the chambers. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of the endocardium inside the heart chambers?

options.A: Providing a smooth surface to prevent abnormal blood clotting
options.B: Supplying oxygen directly to the heart muscle cells
options.C: Anchoring the heart securely inside the thoracic cavity
options.D: Producing serous fluid to reduce friction during movement

explanation: The endocardium is a smooth endothelial lining that prevents platelets from sticking and forming clots inside the active heart chambers. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which heart valve separates the left atrium from the left ventricle?
explanation: The mitral valve, also called the bicuspid valve, guards the opening between the left atrium and left ventricle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: Blood passing directly through the tricuspid valve is heading to which structure?
explanation: The tricuspid valve directs blood flow from the right atrium down into the right ventricle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h3)

question: Where do the coronary arteries originate from?
explanation: Coronary arteries branch off the ascending aorta to deliver freshly oxygenated blood to the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why can the heart muscle not rely solely on the blood inside its own chambers for oxygen?

options.A: Endocardial cells block all nutrients from reaching the muscle layer
options.B: The myocardial wall is too thick for direct diffusion from the chambers
options.C: Valves prevent blood from touching the interior walls of the ventricles
options.D: The blood inside the right side of the heart contains zero oxygen

explanation: Cardiac muscle tissue is thick and dense, requiring a dedicated network of coronary vessels for its own blood supply. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which structure serves as the primary natural pacemaker of the heart?
explanation: The sinoatrial node sets the normal baseline rhythm of the heart by generating spontaneous electrical impulses. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the functional role of the Purkinje fibers in the conduction system?

options.A: Carrying deoxygenated blood away from the cardiac muscle
options.B: Delaying the electrical signal to allow complete atrial filling
options.C: Generating the initial pacemaker impulse in the right atrium
options.D: Spreading electrical impulses rapidly through the ventricular myocardium

explanation: Purkinje fibers ensure the rapid, synchronized contraction of the ventricles from the bottom up. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h5)

question: What physiological event causes the first heart sound, or 'lub'?

options.A: Opening of the aortic and pulmonary valves

explanation: The closure of the tricuspid and mitral valves at the start of ventricular systole creates the first heart sound. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: During which phase of the cardiac cycle do the ventricles fill with blood?
explanation: During diastole, the heart muscle relaxes, allowing blood to flow freely from the atria into the ventricles. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h6)

question: How is cardiac output calculated?

options.A: Blood pressure divided by vascular resistance
options.B: Stroke volume divided by heart rate
options.C: Heart rate multiplied by stroke volume
options.D: Heart rate plus systolic blood pressure

explanation: Cardiac output equals the heart rate multiplied by the volume of blood ejected per beat. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary function of baroreceptors located in the carotid sinus?

options.A: Releasing hormones to stimulate red blood cell production
options.B: Detecting changes in blood pressure and signaling vasomotor centers
options.C: Measuring blood oxygen and carbon dioxide levels directly
options.D: Filtering waste products out of the circulating plasma

explanation: Baroreceptors monitor arterial stretch and help regulate blood pressure reflexively through autonomic adjustments. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h7)

question: Which blood vessel type is primarily responsible for nutrient and gas exchange with tissues?
explanation: Capillaries have extremely thin walls that allow easy diffusion of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)

question: Why do veins contain one-way valves along their pathway?

options.A: To prevent the backflow of blood against gravity
options.B: To regulate local vascular resistance in peripheral tissues
options.C: To withstand the high-pressure surges from the left ventricle
options.D: To filter pathogens out of the returning blood supply

explanation: One-way valves in veins ensure blood flows consistently back toward the heart, especially from the lower limbs. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h8)
